title: Stream offset anchoring for replayed and truncated responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe ambiguous token counts when long-lived streaming sessions are interrupted, replayed by proxies, or truncated by clients. In a few recent incidents customers received overcharges or undercounts because the metering pipeline could not deterministically decide which fragments were final and which were speculative replays.

Scope: Design and implement an "anchoring" protocol and ledger semantics that allow: (1) deterministic finalization of token counts for streams that are truncated or replayed, (2) provisional accounting during live streams for quota enforcement, and (3) low-latency path for optimistic credits while preserving auditability. This ticket covers protocol changes between edge proxies -> session manager -> metering ledger, runtime changes to annotate outbound chunks with anchors, and the ledger commit/rollback rules.

Goals:
- No double-charging for replayed fragments across common proxy patterns.
- Consistent final token counts regardless of midstream model handoffs or client truncation.
- Minimal latency regression for the hot path (<=5% token latency budget impact).
- Clear audit trail that ties ledger entries to session anchors for debugging and retroactive correction.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits an anchor token (opaque 64-bit marker) with every chunk boundary and the runtime persists anchor -> cumulative token delta mapping.

Ledger only treats entries as final when an anchored terminal marker or explicit finalization event is observed; provisional debits are visible but labeled 'provisional' in the billing UI and queryable via audit APIs.
Replayed fragments with identical anchor sequences do not produce duplicate final charges; at most provisional credits are adjusted and reconciled only once.
Unit and integration test suite that simulates truncated sessions, proxy replays, multi-tenant multiplexing and asserts identical final token counts under 1000 randomized scenarios.
Benchmark shows <5% tail increase in token attribution latency on a standard dedupe path compared to baseline without anchoring (test harness: runtime-1.22/staging cluster).
Confluence design doc and a security review sign-off exist and are linked from the ticket.
implementation_notes: Protocol: add optional 'anchor_id' (opaque hex string) to the streaming frame metadata emitted by the runtime on chunk flush. Anchor is monotonic per-session and included in session checkpoint snapshots.
Metering: store provisional ledger entries keyed by (session_id, anchor_id). Final commit occurs on receipt of a terminal anchor or explicit finalize message from the session manager.
Rollback: if an anchor sequence is observed to be replayed (same anchor_id already committed), discard duplicate provisional entries and emit reconciliation audit record.

Rate limiter: treat provisional debits as soft reservations against quota windows. On final commit, convert provisional to hard debits; on rollback, return soft reservations and adjust burst counters.
Compatibility: anchors are backward-compatible (runtime falls back to current behavior when anchor metadata absent). We will gate enforcement behind a feature flag 'anchor-metering' per-tenant.
Storage: anchors and provisional entries are TTL'd at 7 days but retained longer in archival store for audits. Evaluate storage cost and compaction strategy as part of follow-up.
tests: Deterministic replay test: Simulate a proxy replaying a subset of chunks; final ledger must match non-replayed run.
Truncation test: Client terminates without sending finalize; session manager triggers graceful finalize after TTL and ledger matches expected truncated count.
Concurrent multiplexer test: Two tenants multiplexed over same connection should have independent anchors and isolated provisional ledger entries.
Rate limiter interaction: Provisional debits should prevent quota oversubscription; stress test at 10k sessions/s with random truncation pattern.
Performance microbench: Measure added CPU and latency for anchor generation and ledger writes under production load (p95 and p99).
comments: 2025-02-04 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes. Spike planned to prototype anchor_id encoding and measure overhead. Assigned Marco for implementation and Sara (infra) for ledger model changes.

2025-02-06 - Marco Chen: Spike results: anchor generation ~35ns/op, additional 1.8% p95 latency in the hot path when persisted synchronously. Proposed async persistence for provisional entries to hit <1% impact.

2025-02-07 - Design review (PM+SRE+Sec): PM requests provisional entries be surfaced in Console cost breakdown as 'estimated'. SRE requests a reconciliation job to reconcile provisional vs final daily and expose diffs to billing alerts.

2025-02-09 - Security review note: potential information leakage if anchor IDs are predictable. Decided to use per-session HMAC(seed || monotonic_counter) to make anchors unguessable. Security owner: Leah Morris.
2025-02-11 - QA: Add integration tests for mixed legacy/anchored runtimes. Action: create a toggle at proxy ingress to inject anchors for testing replay scenarios.

2025-02-12 - Marco Chen: Implemented feature-flagged path; opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7142 and design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Stream+Offset+Anchoring. Requesting review from SRE and Billing engineers.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy anchor emission to staging with feature flag off for ledger commit (anchors emitted but provisional entries not persisted).
Stage 2: Enable provisional persistence in staging; run 24h reconciliation job and compare with baseline billing ledger.
Stage 3: Canary on 5% tenant traffic in production with 'anchor-metering' flag; observe Console diffs and reconciliation alerts for 72h.
Stage 4: Full rollout with daily reconciliation and alerting; schedule billing team review before conversion of provisional -> final for billed invoices.
